IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p189#4/r4.claim: Meccans objected that Muhammad said idol worship and killing a protected person would not be forgiven, asking why they should migrate and convert after doing those things.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p189#4/r4.anchor: فكيف نهاجر ونسلم وقد فعلنا ذلك فنزلت هذه الآية وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p189#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p189#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p189#4/r5.claim: Those who have transgressed against themselves are people who committed major sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p189#4/r5.anchor: ومعنى أسرفوا على أنفسهم ارتكبوا الكبائر

BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r1.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r1.claim: Al-Raghib defines excess as crossing the limit in anything a person does, though the word is most familiar for excessive spending; the verse includes money and other matters.
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r1.anchor: قال الراغب : السرف تجاوز الحد في كل ما يفعله الإنسان

BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r2.claim: The preposition على carries the sense of committing an offense against oneself: they went too far in sin, major sins, and indecencies.
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r2.anchor: وتعدية الإسراف بعلى لتضمين معنى الجناية ، والمعنى : أفرطوا في الجناية

BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r3.speaker: البيضاوي ومن تبعه
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r3.claim: Al-Baydawi and followers say that the possessive address My servants conventionally restricts the verse to believers in Qur'anic usage.
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r3.anchor: قال البيضاوي ومن تبعه : إضافة العباد تخصصه بالمؤمن

BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r4.claim: Bursevi rejects that restriction by citing 17:5, where servants of God refers to Nebuchadnezzar and his people, whom commentators agree were unbelievers; he allows that a distinction between mediated and unmediated possession could be proposed.
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r4.anchor: وكانوا كفارا بالإتفاق إلا أن يدعي الفرق

BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r5.speaker: الوسيط
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r5.claim: Al-Wasit says commentators connect the revelation to people afraid their grave past sins, including idolatry, murder, adultery, hostility to the Prophet, and fighting him, would not be forgiven if they converted; the Prophet rejoiced and Companions called it among the broadest forgiveness verses.

BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r6.speaker: التكملة
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r6.claim: Al-Takmila recounts that Wahshi, who killed Hamza, asked the Prophet if he could repent; after hearing successive assurances concerning repentance and God's forgiveness, he feared exclusion from the divine will, then this verse was revealed and he converted.
BURSEVI:v8p93#2/r6.anchor: روي : أن وحشيا قاتل حمزة رضي الله عنه كتب إلى النبي عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r1.claim: Although the occasion is particular, the wording applies generally and includes every person who has sinned excessively.
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r1.anchor: وعلى كل تقدير فخصوص السبب لا ينافي عموم اللفظ

BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r2.claim: Qunut is the greatest form of despair.

BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r3.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r3.claim: Al-Mufradat defines qunut as despair of good.
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r3.anchor: اليأس من الخير. وبالفارسية : (نوميدشدن از خير)

BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r4.claim: Divine mercy means beneficence, giving, and gracious favor; in the order of existence it follows forgiveness, which first shields the servant from punishment.
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r4.anchor: والرحمة من الله تعالى الإنعام والإعطاء والتفضل

BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r5.claim: Thus the command means first do not despair of God's forgiveness and then of his further favor.
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r5.anchor: ولذا قالوا في المعنى : لا تيأسوا من مغفرته أولا

BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r6.claim: A Persian maxim warns against hopelessness, calling despair a form of unbelief.
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r6.anchor: لا تيأسوا من مغفرته أولا وتفضله ثانيا

BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r7.claim: Al-Maʿalim al-Tanzil recounts Ibn Masud rebuking a preacher who focused on Hell, chains, and shackles for making people despair and asking whether he had read God's merciful declaration.
BURSEVI:v8p93#3/r7.anchor: كه ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه در مسجد در آمد ديد كه واعظى

BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r1.claim: Despair signals lost spiritual receptivity and a broken bond with God; any remnant of original light would perceive mercy, which precedes wrath, and hope to receive it despite sin.
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r1.anchor: واعلم أن القنوط من رحمة الله علامة زوال الاستعداد

BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r2.claim: Despair, unlike qunut rooted in some remaining light, indicates total veiling and a blackened face.
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r2.anchor: وأما اليأس ، فدليل الاحتجاب الكلي واسوداد الوجه

BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r3.claim: Forgiveness of all sins presupposes that the heart retains the light of divine unity; without it the person falls under 4:48, and despair is among the greatest calamities.
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r3.anchor: فالله تعالى يغفر الذنوب جميعا بشرط بقاء نور التوحيد في القلب

BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r4.claim: God graciously gives servants until the death rattle; whoever returns to God before the final breath can still repent.
BURSEVI:v8p93#4/r4.anchor: وقد أمهل تعالى عباده تفضلا منه إلى وقت الغرغرة

BURSEVI:v8p94/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p94/r1.claim: The promise answers why people must not despair: God forgives all sins, even innumerable minor or major ones, either by pardon or after some punishment, as he wills.
BURSEVI:v8p94/r1.anchor: كأنه قيل : ما سبب النهي عن القنوط من الرحمة فأجيب بأن سبب النهي هو

BURSEVI:v8p94/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p94/r2.claim: The universal wording is qualified: consensus excludes idolatry, and the sinner's forgiveness is subject to divine will by applying the unrestricted statement to restricted evidence.
BURSEVI:v8p94/r2.anchor: والعموم بمعنى الخصوص ؛ لأن الشرك ليس بداخل في الآية إجماعا

BURSEVI:v8p94/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v8p94/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says God forgives all sins without concern, for he is the forgiving and merciful.
BURSEVI:v8p94/r3.anchor: إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا ولا يبالي إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

BURSEVI:v8p94/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94/r4.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v8p94/r4.claim: A Prophetic couplet asks God to forgive fully, since no servant is without sin.
BURSEVI:v8p94/r4.anchor: إن تغفر اللهم ، فاغفر جما ، وأي عبد لك لا ألما

BURSEVI:v8p94/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94/r5.speaker: الشيخ الكبير
BURSEVI:v8p94/r5.claim: The Shaykh al-Akbar distinguishes pardon, which erases sin as in 11:114, from forgiveness, which can transform evil deeds into good as in 25:70.
BURSEVI:v8p94/r5.anchor: والفرق بين العفو والمغفرة هو أن حقيقة العفو هو المحو

BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r1.claim: Al-Ghafur signifies erasing what causes punishment, while al-Rahim signifies bestowing reward; their intensive forms answer the multitude of sins, forgiveness, and mercy.
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r1.anchor: الأول : إشارة إلى محو ما يوجب العقاب

BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r2.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r2.claim: Al-Qushayri reads My servants as honor and their excess as blame: sinners bow their heads until the divine address lifts them, while the self-assured obedient lower theirs.
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r2.anchor: قال الأستاذ القشيري قدس سره : التسمية بيا عبادي مدح

BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r3.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r3.claim: Al-Qushayri finds renewed hope in the phrase على أنفسهم: even the one who repeatedly came to God's door must not despair or weary of turning to him.
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r3.anchor: يعني : إن أسرفت لا تقنط من رحمة الله

BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r4.claim: The definite article in sins is exhaustive, reinforced by all: God forgives without leaving anything and can meet vast sin with ancient care.
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r4.anchor: والألف واللام في الذنوب للاستغراق ، والعموم جميعا

BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r5.claim: The cited Kashf al-Asrar contrasts angels' pure servitude with humans' servitude and love, presenting love as the distinctive honor given to humans and as the basis for their elevated rank.
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r5.anchor: (بدانكه از آفريد كان حق تعالى كمال كرامت دوكروه راست

BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r6.claim: In the same Kashf al-Asrar passage, God keeps human beings' possessive title My servants despite their sins, veils their faults through love, and speaks of their excess generally rather than exposing particular sins.
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r6.anchor: نه بينى كه زلت برايشان قضا كرد وبآن همه زلات نام عبوديت از ايشان نيفكند

BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r7.speaker: موسى عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r7.claim: In the Kashf al-Asrar account, Moses asks how God can will disobedience while hating it and the servant who commits it; God says this establishes his pardon, whose treasury would otherwise go unused.
BURSEVI:v8p94#2/r7.anchor: موسى عليه السلام كفت "إلهي تريد المعصية من العباد وتبغضها"

BURSEVI:v8p95/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p95/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p95/r1.claim: Bursevi reports that on Judgment Day God tells some sinful believers he concealed their sins in worldly life and will forgive them now, evidence for forgiveness without repentance.
BURSEVI:v8p95/r1.anchor: روي : أن الله تعالى يقول يوم القيامة لبعض عصاة المؤمنين

BURSEVI:v8p95/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p95/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p95/r2.claim: Bursevi distinguishes idolatry from other sins by saying an unbeliever does not seek pardon for his wrongdoing.
BURSEVI:v8p95/r2.anchor: والفرق بين الشرك وسائر المعصية هو أن الكافر لا يطلب العفو

BURSEVI:v8p95/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p95/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p95/r3.claim: He reads 4:17 as applying to repentance near death: at the death rattle neither idolatry nor other sins are forgiven, even with repentance; this does not preclude pardon of non-idolatrous sins without repentance earlier, while idolatry's forgiveness would violate wisdom.
BURSEVI:v8p95/r3.anchor: إنما هو بالنسبة إلى حال الغرغرة ، فالشرك وسائر المعاصي لا يغفر

BURSEVI:v8p95/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p95/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v8p95/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that God made mercy one hundred parts, retained ninety-nine, and sent one to earth; even a mare lifts her hoof to spare her foal. Bursevi draws encouragement from the many visible and hidden blessings of this single earthly portion and the promise of a hundredfold in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v8p95/r4.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه ، قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v8p95/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p95/r5.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
BURSEVI:v8p95/r5.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh says the Qur'an contains treasures that compel pardon for all believers, including this verse; scholars therefore call it the Qur'an's most hopeful verse for monotheists.
BURSEVI:v8p95/r5.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ رحمه الله : في كتاب الله كنوز موجبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r1.claim: The verse calls all sinners, disbelievers included, to repent and return; God forgives every sin for those who repent, however grave or numerous their sins, even like sea foam.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r1.anchor: هذه الآية الكريمة دعوة لجميع العصاة من الكفرة وغيرهم إلى التوبة والإنابة، وإخبار بأن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن تاب منها ورجع عنها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r2.claim: It cannot mean forgiveness without repentance, because shirk is not forgiven for someone who dies without repenting of it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r2.anchor: ولا يصح حمل هذه [الآية] (1) على غير توبة (2) ؛ لأن الشرك لا يغفر لمن لم يتب منه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that polytheists who had killed and committed adultery repeatedly asked Muhammad whether their past deeds had expiation; 25:68 and this verse were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس (3) [رضي الله عنهما] (4) ؛ أن ناسا من أهل الشرك كانوا قد قتلوا فأكثروا، وزنوا فأكثروا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r4.speaker: ثوبان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r4.claim: Ahmad reports Thawban saying the verse was dearer to the Prophet than the world and all it contains; when asked whether it included a polytheist, he affirmed this three times.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r4.anchor: ثوبان -مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم-يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "ما أحب أن لي الدنيا وما فيها بهذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r5.speaker: عمرو بن عبسة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r5.claim: Ahmad reports that the Prophet forgave an old man who confessed many betrayals and sins after he affirmed God's oneness and Muhammad's prophethood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p106/r5.anchor: عن (13) عمرو بن عبسة (14) قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، شيخ كبير يدعم على عصا له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r1.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r1.claim: Asma bint Yazid reports the Prophet reciting 11:46 and then 39:53, with the added phrase 'and He does not mind'; Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r1.anchor: عن أسماء بنت يزيد (2) قالت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ: {إنه عمل غير صالح}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r2.claim: These reports teach that God forgives all such sins with repentance and that no servant should despair, however grave or numerous the sins, because repentance and mercy remain open.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r2.anchor: فهذه الأحاديث كلها دالة على أن المراد: أنه يغفر جميع ذلك مع التوبة، ولا يقنطن (4) عبد من رحمة الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r3.claim: He supports the breadth of repentance with verses on God accepting repentance, forgiving the sinner who seeks forgiveness, welcoming repentant hypocrites and former disbelievers, and those who repent after persecution.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r3.anchor: قال الله تعالى: {ألم يعلموا أن الله هو يقبل التوبة عن عباده} [التوبة:104] ، وقال تعالى: {ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r4.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri marvels at God's generosity: people killed His allies, yet He still invites them to repent and receive forgiveness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r4.anchor: قال الحسن البصري: انظر (5) إلى هذا الكرم والجود، قتلوا أولياءه وهو يدعوهم إلى التوبة والمغفرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r5.claim: In the Sahihayn, Abu Sa'id reports a killer who murdered ninety-nine, completed one hundred after a monk denied repentance, then asked a learned man who directed him to migrate to a town of worshipers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r5.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أبي سعيد، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، حديث الذي (6) قتل تسعا (7) وتسعين نفسا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r6.claim: The man died on the way; mercy and punishment angels disputed over him, and God ordered a measurement that found him a span nearer the destination, so mercy's angels took him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r6.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أبي سعيد، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، حديث الذي (6) قتل تسعا (7) وتسعين نفسا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r7.claim: The narration adds that the dying man shifted his chest toward the good town, so God brought it nearer and moved the town he was leaving farther away.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p107/r7.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أبي سعيد، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، حديث الذي (6) قتل تسعا (7) وتسعين نفسا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God invites even people making extreme claims about Jesus, Ezra, divine poverty or restraint, and the Trinity to repentance, then cites Pharaoh’s still greater claims as another case covered by mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، رضي الله عنهما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says anyone who makes God’s servants despair of repentance after this has rejected God’s Book, though a servant cannot repent until God enables and accepts his repentance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس [رضي الله عنهما] (4) من آيس عباد الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r3.claim: Ibn Masud’s report ranks 39:53 as the Quran’s most hope-giving verse; it also ranks 2:255 greatest, 16:90 most comprehensive of good and evil, and 65:2–3 most forceful in its promise of an exit and provision; Masruq agrees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r3.anchor: سمعت ابن مسعود يقول إن أعظم آية في كتاب الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r4.claim: Ibn Masud rebukes a preacher for making people despair and recites this verse; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits the report from al-A'mash, Abu Sa'id and Abu al-Kanud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r4.anchor: مر عبد الله -يعني ابن مسعود-على قاص، وهو يذكر الناس، فقال: يا مذكر لم تقنط

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r5.claim: The Prophet says that even sins filling the space between heaven and earth are forgiven if people seek God’s forgiveness, and that God would bring sinners who repent if people never sinned; Ahmad alone transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r5.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "والذي نفسي بيده، لو أخطأتم حتى تملأ خطاياكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r6.claim: Abu Ayyub says near death that he had concealed the Prophet’s assurance: if people did not sin, God would create a people who sin and then be forgiven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p108/r6.anchor: قد كنت كتمت منكم شيئا سمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "لولا أنكم تذنبون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r1.claim: The Abu Ayyub report is transmitted by Ahmad, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi through Qutayba and al-Layth; Muslim also gives a route through Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi from Abu Sirma, the Companion Abu Ayyub. No grading is stated here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r1.anchor: رواه الإمام أحمد، وأخرجه مسلم في صحيحه، والترمذي جميعا، عن قتيبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet’s sayings that regret is the atonement for sin and that God would bring sinners whom He forgives if people did not sin; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس (4) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كفارة الذنب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r3.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said God loves the servant who repeatedly falls into error and repents; Ibn Kathir says the canonical compilers did not transmit it by this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r3.anchor: علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله يحب العبد المفتن التواب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r4.claim: A report from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr recounts Satan’s escalating requests for power over Adam’s descendants, Adam’s appeal for protection, God’s provision of a guardian and multiplied good deeds, and repentance remaining open while the soul is in the body; it ends with 39:53.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير قال: إن إبليس -عليه لعائن الله-قال: يا رب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109#2/r1.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109#2/r1.claim: Umar relates that some Muslims who had reverted to unbelief under persecution thought God would accept neither expiation nor repentance, even from themselves; after the Prophet reached Medina, 39:53–55 was revealed concerning them. Umar sent it to Hisham ibn al-As, who understood it as applying to their despair, then traveled to Medina and joined the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمير، عن عمر، رضي الله عنه، في حديثه قال: وكنا نقول

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r8.claim: Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb read taqniṭū with kasra on the nūn.
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r8.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب: تقنطوا بكسر النون

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r9.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r9.claim: The other readers use fatḥa on the nūn; both forms are dialect variants.

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r10.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r10.claim: Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī is also reported to read the nūn with ḍamma.

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r11.claim: The verb has two conjugational patterns, qaniṭa yaqnaṭu and qaniṭa yaqniṭu.
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r11.anchor: يقال: قنط يقنط، نحو: ضرب يضرب، وقنط يقنط نحو: حمد يحمد.

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r12.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim read yā ʿibādi with fatḥa on the final yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r12.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم: ياعبادي بفتح الياء

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r13.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r13.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb, with some transmissions from ʿĀṣim, read without that fatḥa.
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وعاصم في بعض الروايات ويعقوب بغير فتح

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r14.claim: All readers retain the yāʾ when stopping because it is in the codex, except Abū Bakr's transmission from ʿĀṣim.
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r14.anchor: وكلهم يقفون عليه بإثبات الياء؛ لأنها ثابتة في المصحف إلا في رواية أبي بكر عن عاصم أنه يقف بغير ياء

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r15.claim: Isrāf is going beyond the limit.

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r16.claim: Qunūṭ is despairing of mercy; despair rests on certainty, while hope rests on possibility.
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r16.anchor: والقنوط: اليأس من الرحمة، واليأس مع اليقين، والرجاء مع التجويز.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r1.claim: Those who exceeded bounds against themselves are people who committed sins excessively.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r1.anchor: جنوا عليها بالإسراف في المعاصي والغلو فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r2.claim: The verb is read with the nūn bearing fatḥa, kasra, or ḍamma.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r3.claim: Forgiveness is conditional on repentance; the Qur’an repeats this condition, and as one coherent discourse cannot contradict itself, it applies even where unstated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r3.anchor: يعني بشرط التوبة ، وقد تكرر ذكر هذا الشرط في القرآن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r4.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd adds for whom He wills; al-Zamakhsharī says this means those who repent, since divine will follows wisdom and justice.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن عباس وابن مسعود : ( يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفاطمة رضي الله عنها
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r5.claim: Another reported reading attributed to the Prophet and Fāṭima adds and He does not care.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r5.anchor: في قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفاطمة رضي الله عنها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r6.claim: The denial of concern is compared with the Qur’anic denial of fear in 91:15.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r6.anchor: ونظير نفي المبالاة نفي الخوف في قوله تعالى : { ولا يخاف عقباها }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r7.claim: One occasion report says Meccans asked how they could emigrate after worshipping idols and killing a person God forbade killing, since they thought Muḥammad said they could not be forgiven.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r7.anchor: قال أهل مكة : يزعم محمد أن من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r8.speaker: عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r8.claim: Another occasion report concerns ʿAyyāsh b. Abī Rabīʿa, al-Walīd b. al-Walīd, and others who accepted Islam, were tortured into apostasy, then received this verse through ʿUmar and returned to Islam and emigrated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r8.anchor: أسلم عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر معهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r9.claim: A further opinion says the verse was revealed about Waḥshī, who killed Ḥamza.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r9.anchor: نزلت في وحشي قاتل حمزة رضي الله عنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r10.claim: The Prophet prized the verse above the world and all it contains; when asked whether it included one who associated partners, he affirmed that it did, repeating this three times.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p138/r10.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 970 ) ( ما أحب أن لي الدنيا وما فيها بهذه الآية )

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r1.claim: The phrase first means exceeding bounds through associating partners with God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r1.anchor: أي أسرفوا على أنفسهم في الشرك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r2.claim: Another possibility is sins committed while retaining faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r2.anchor: ويحتمل ثانيا : أسرفوا على أنفسهم في ارتكاب الذنوب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r3.claim: The command means not to despair of God's mercy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r4.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says God forgives through repentance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r4.anchor: أحدها : يغفرها بالتوبة منها , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r5.claim: Another view says God pardons sins except shirk.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r5.anchor: الثاني : يغفرها بالعفو عنها إلا الشرك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r6.claim: A third view says God forgives minor sins when major sins are avoided.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r7.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r7.claim: Hasan and al-Kalbi say this and the next verse were revealed about Wahshi, killer of Hamza.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r7.anchor: قيل نزلت هذه الآية والتي بعدها في وحشي قاتل حمزة , قاله الحسن والكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r8.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r8.claim: Ali says no Qur'an verse is broader in promise than this one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r8.anchor: وقال علي عليه السلام : ما في القرآن آية أوسع منها

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r9.speaker: ثوبان
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r9.claim: Thawban says he heard the Prophet say he would not trade the world for this verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r9.anchor: وروى ثوبان قال : سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

MUJAHID:v2p559#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p559#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p559#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the servants who exceeded the limits against themselves are those who killed people in the pre-Islamic period.
MUJAHID:v2p559#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله عز وجل ﴿ يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم ﴾ يعني من قتل الأنفس في الجاهلية

MUQATIL:39:52-54/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r4.claim: This was revealed about Meccan polytheists after Wahshi, client of al-Mut‘im ibn ‘Adi ibn Nawfal, asked how to repent. After 25:68 and 25:70 were revealed, he accepted Islam; Meccans objected that his repentance was accepted but theirs was not addressed.
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r4.anchor: فقال وحشى، مولى المطعم بن عدى بن نوفل: إنى قد فعلت هذه الخصال فكيف لى بالتوبة

MUQATIL:39:52-54/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r5.claim: Their excess means shirk, murder, and adultery; no sin is greater excess than shirk.
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r5.anchor: يعنى بالإسراف: الشرك والقتل والزنا فلا ذنب أعظم إسرافا من الشرك

MUQATIL:39:52-54/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r6.claim: Do not despair of God’s mercy, as they thought they had no repentance.
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r6.anchor: يقول: لا تيأسوا { من رحمة الله } لأنهم ظنوا ألا توبة لهم

MUQATIL:39:52-54/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r7.claim: For those who repent, God forgives the sins mentioned in al-Furqan—shirk, murder, adultery—and calls them to repent.
MUQATIL:39:52-54/r7.anchor: يعنى الشرك والقتل والزنا الذى ذكر فى سورة الفرقان { إنه هو الغفور الرحيم } [آية: 53] لمن تاب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r1.speaker: بصرى وحمزة وعلى
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r1.claim: The Basran, Ḥamza, and ʿAlī readings leave the yāʾ of yā ʿibādī quiescent.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r2.claim: They wronged themselves by exceeding limits in sins.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r2.anchor: جنوا عليها بالاسراف فى المعاصى والغلو فيها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r3.claim: La taqnaṭū means do not despair; a variant with kasra on the nūn is read by ʿAlī and the Basrans.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r3.anchor: لا تيأسوا وبكسر النون على وبصرى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r4.claim: God forgives all sins by pardon, with shirk excepted.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r4.anchor: ﴿ من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا ﴾ بالعفو عنها إلا الشرك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r5.claim: A Prophetic reading adds that God forgives all sins and does not care, an expression compared with the Qur'anic wording that He does not fear the consequence.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r5.anchor: وفي قراءة النبى عليه السلام يغفر الذنوب جميعا ولا يبالى ونظير نفى المبالاة نفى الخوف فى قوله ولا يخاف عقباها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r6.claim: One account says the verse was revealed concerning Waḥshī, who killed Ḥamza.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r6.anchor: قيل نزلت فى وحشى قاتل حمزة رضى الله عنه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r7.claim: The Messenger said he would not exchange this verse for the whole world and everything in it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r7.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أحب أن لى الدنيا وما فيها بهذه الآية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r8.claim: Al-Ghafūr covers grave sins, while al-Raḥīm removes terrible griefs.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p59#4/r8.anchor: ﴿ إنه هو الغفور ﴾ بستر عظائم الذنوب ﴿ الرحيم ﴾ بكشف فظائع الكروب

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r1.claim: The vocative form yā ʿibādī may also be written without the final yāʾ, since vocatives allow that deletion.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r1.anchor: وإن شئت حذفت الياء لأن النداء موضع حذف.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r2.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r2.claim: Umar reports that he, ʿAyyāsh and Hishām planned to migrate; Hishām was detained and fell into persecution. They and the Muslims thought there was no repentance for them, until this passage through 39:60 was revealed. Umar sent it to Hishām, who understood, returned and rejoined the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r2.anchor: عن عمر قال: لما اجتمعنا على الهجرة، اتعدت أنا وهشام بن العاصي بن وائل السهمي،

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that polytheists who had killed and committed adultery in great numbers asked whether they could repent; this verse was revealed in response, as Bukhari relates in meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r3.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: كان قوم من المشركين قتلوا فأكثروا، وزنوا فأكثروا،

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās places the revelation among Meccans who feared that idolatry and killing made migration and conversion unacceptable.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا نزلت في أهل مكة قالوا: يزعم محمد أن من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r5.claim: One view says the verse concerned Muslims who had been excessive in worship and feared that earlier sins from the pre-Islamic period would prevent acceptance.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r5.anchor: وقيل: إنها نزلت في قوم من المسلمين أسرفوا على أنفسهم في العبادة، وخافوا ألا يتقبل منهم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAṭāʾ say the verse was revealed about Waḥshī, who killed Ḥamza and thought God would not accept his conversion; the next segment gives his encounter with the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وعطاء: نزلت في وحشي قاتل حمزة لأنه ظن أن الله لا يقبل إسلامه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r1.claim: In the account attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās through Ibn Jurayj and ʿAṭāʾ, Waḥshī sought the Prophet’s protection to hear God’s words and asked whether repentance could cover idolatry, murder and adultery. The Prophet recited 25:68 onward, then 4:48; after Waḥshī feared he might not be among those God wills to forgive, 39:53 was revealed and he accepted Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r1.anchor: أتى وحشي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا محمد أتيتك مستجيرا فأجرني

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r2.speaker: أسماء
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r2.claim: Asmāʾ reports that she heard the Prophet recite this verse with the wording that God forgives all sins and is the Forgiving, Merciful.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r2.anchor: وروى حماد بن سلمة عن ثابت عن شهر بن حوشب عن أسماء: أنها سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s codex has the added words “for whom He wills”; al-Naḥḥās treats this and the recitation reported from Asmāʾ as exegetical readings meaning that God forgives whomever He wills.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r3.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود { إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء }.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r4.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says the ones God has identified as forgiven are the repentant and those who committed a minor sin without a major one; the following command to turn back shows repentance is intended.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r4.anchor: وقد عرف الله عز وجل من شاء أن يغفر له، وهو التائب أو من عمل صغيرة ولم تكن له كبيرة،

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r5.claim: The repentant person’s sins are all forgiven, as shown by God’s promise to forgive whoever repents.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r5.anchor: فالتائب مغفور له ذنوبه جميعا، يدل على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r6.claim: ʿAlī says no verse in the Qur’an is broader in its promise than this one.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r6.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: ما في القرآن آية أوسع من هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar calls this the most hopeful verse in the Qur’an; Ibn ʿAbbās’s reply follows in the next segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:53-54/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر: وهذه أرجى آية في القرآن فرد عليهم ابن عباس وقال أرجى آية في القرآن قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r1.claim: The passage quotes God’s promise of forgiveness for people despite wrongdoing, the counterexample to Ibn ʿUmar’s view cited in the preceding segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r1.anchor: وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم [الرعد: 6] وقد مضى في «الرعد».

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r2.claim: Both kasra and fatḥa on the nūn of taqnaṭū are reported; al-Qurṭubī refers readers to his earlier note on 15:56.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r2.anchor: وقرىء «ولا تقنطوا» بكسر النون وفتحها. وقد مضى في «الحجر» بيانه.

QASHANI:39:53/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:53/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:53/r1.claim: Despair signals lost spiritual aptitude, departure from primordial nature through veiling, and severed connection with God; retaining a trace of original light lets even a deeply wayward person recognize mercy and hope for its reach.
QASHANI:39:53/r1.anchor: فإن القنوط علامة زوال الاستعداد والسقوط عن الفطرة بالاحتجاب

QASHANI:39:53/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:53/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:53/r2.claim: Only total veiling brings despair: turning from the upper world and being covered by the material veil of created nature.
QASHANI:39:53/r2.anchor: وإنما اليأس لا يكون إلا مع الاحتجاب الكلي واسوداد الوجه بالإعراض عن العالم العلوي

QASHANI:39:53/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:53/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:53/r3.claim: Forgiveness of all sins is conditional on the heart retaining the light of monotheism; the address as God's servants signals their relation to Him.
QASHANI:39:53/r3.anchor: بشرط بقاء نور التوحيد في القلب

QASHANI:39:53/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:53/r4.speaker: قيل
QASHANI:39:53/r4.claim: It is said that God forgives all sins for the monotheists of Muhammad's community, unlike other communities; Noah's people are told He will forgive them some sins.
QASHANI:39:53/r4.anchor: ولهذا قيل: يغفر جميعها للأمة المحمدية الموحدين دون سائر الأمم

QASHANI:39:53/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:53/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:53/r5.claim: The Forgiving removes dispositions of excess and deficiency, while the Merciful bestows virtues.
QASHANI:39:53/r5.anchor: الفغور } لهئيات الرذائل من الإفراط والتفريط

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r1.claim: Repentance remains obligatory and fear of punishment remains because sinners cannot know punishment is wholly removed: God may forgive outright or forgive after a period in Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r1.anchor: عندنا التوبة واجبة وخوف العقاب قائم

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r2.claim: Calling sinners servants evokes their need, humility, and poverty, qualities that invite a generous Lord to give mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r2.anchor: المذنب بالعبد والعبودية مفسرة بالحاجة والذلة والمسكنة

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r3.claim: God’s possessive attribution of the sinners to Himself honors them and reassures them against punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r4.claim: The damage of sins returns to the sinners themselves, so they need no additional harm imposed on them.
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r4.anchor: ومعناه أن ضرر تلك الذنوب ما عاد إليه

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r5.claim: Forbidding despair commands hope, and a generous Lord’s command to hope is a promise of generosity.
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r5.anchor: نهاهم عن القنوط فيكون هذا أمرا بالرجاء والكريم إذا أمر بالرجاء فلا يليق به إلا الكرم

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r6.claim: The verse says “God’s mercy” rather than “My mercy,” invoking God’s greatest name and therefore the greatest kind of mercy and favor.
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r6.anchor: لأن قولنا الله أعظم أسماء الله وأجلها

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r7.claim: Repeating God’s name and adding the emphatic particle إن intensifies the promise of mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r7.anchor: بل أعاد اسم الله وقرن به لفظة إن المفيدة لأعظم وجوه التأكيد

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r8.claim: The word “all” reinforces the comprehensive promise of forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r8.anchor: فقال جميعا وهذا أيضا من المؤكدات

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r9.claim: “The Forgiving” signals removal of grounds for punishment, while “the Merciful” signals the granting of grounds for mercy and reward.
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r9.anchor: إشارة إلى تحصيل موجبات الرحمة والثواب

RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r10.claim: The emphatic pronoun yields exclusivity: only God is truly forgiving and merciful, displaying perfection in both attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v27p4/r10.anchor: أنه لا غفور ولا رحيم إلا هو

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r1.speaker: أهل مكة
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r1.claim: One reported occasion is that Meccans, having worshipped idols and killed people, wondered how they could accept Islam if Muhammad said such sins would not be forgiven.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r1.anchor: قيل إنها نزلت في أهل مكة فإنهم قالوا يزعم محمد أن من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس لم يغفر له

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r2.speaker: وحشي قاتل حمزة
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r2.claim: Another report says Wahshi, Hamza’s killer, feared his repentance would not be accepted when he wanted to convert; after the verse he embraced Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r2.anchor: نزلت في وحشي قاتل حمزة لما أراد أن يسلم

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r3.claim: When asked whether the promise to Wahshi was exclusive or for Muslims generally, the Prophet replied that it applied generally.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r3.anchor: فقيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه له خاصة أم للمسلمين عامة

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r4.speaker: أناس أصابوا ذنوبا عظاما في الجاهلية
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r4.claim: A further reported occasion is people who committed grave sins in pre-Islamic times and feared Islam would not bring acceptance of their repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r4.anchor: نزلت في أناس أصابوا ذنوبا عظاما في الجاهلية

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r5.speaker: عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r5.claim: The verse was also said to concern Ayyash, al-Walid, and other Muslims who apostatized under persecution; Umar sent them the verses, after which they returned to Islam and emigrated.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r5.anchor: نزلت في عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر من المسلمين أسلموا ثم فتنوا

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r6.claim: Although reports give particular occasions, the general wording governs and the verse is not restricted to those cases.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r6.anchor: العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب فنزول هذه الآيات في هذه الوقائع لا يمنع من عمومها

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r7.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r7.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Asim read the final ya of “عبادي” with fatḥ; the other readers, and some Asim transmissions, do not.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r7.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r8.claim: All readers retain the ya in pausal form except Abu Bakr’s transmission from Asim, which pauses without it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r8.anchor: كلهم يقفون عليه بإثبات الياء لأنها ثابتة في المصحف

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r9.claim: Abu Amr and al-Kisai read the nun in “taqnaṭū” with kasra; the others read it with fatḥa, and both are dialect forms.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي تقنطوا بكسر النون والباقون بفتحها وهما لغتان

RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r10.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud adds “for whom He wills” after the promise to forgive all sins.
RAZI-FULL:v27p5/r10.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن عباس ، وابن مسعود

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r1.claim: The verse echoes 4:110, where a wrongdoer who seeks God's forgiveness finds Him Forgiving and Merciful.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r1.anchor: This verse is similar to 4:110: Whosoever does evil or wrongs himself, and then seeks forgiveness of God

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r2.speaker: many scholars
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r2.claim: Many scholars count this among the Quran's most hopeful verses; the commentary also lists other hopeful verses and says some call these the most joyous.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r2.anchor: Many scholars consider this to be among the most hopeful verses of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r3.claim: The address is understood to encompass all humanity.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r3.anchor: Although this verse addresses all of humanity

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r4.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r4.claim: Some understand the verse as first addressing Makkans who feared they could not repent and follow the Prophet after idolatry, invoking deities, unlawful killing, or fornication.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r4.anchor: many understand it to have initially addressed the situation of some Makkans who feared that they could not repent

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r5.claim: Their prodigality covers every kind of sin, including killing innocent people in the pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r5.anchor: Their being prodigal to the detriment of their own souls would then refer to all manner of sin

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r6.speaker: other commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r6.claim: Another view says it was revealed about Muslims whom the Makkans barred from migrating to Madinah, persecuted into renouncing Islam, and who feared they could not repent.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r6.anchor: Others understand this verse to have been revealed in reference to a small group of Muslims whom the Makkans had prevented from migrating to Madinah

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r7.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r7.claim: Thawbān reports that the Prophet valued this verse above the whole world and everything in it.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r7.anchor: According to Thawbān, a freed slave of the Prophet, the Prophet said, “I would not wish to have the entire world

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r8.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r8.claim: When asked whether forgiveness could include someone who associates partners with God, the Prophet answered three times, “And why not?”
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r8.anchor: The Prophet was silent and then said three times, “And why not one who associates partners with God?”

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r9.claim: Forgiveness of idolatry depends on renouncing it and repenting, as 4:48 and 4:116 state that God does not forgive association of partners.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r9.anchor: Such forgiveness would, however, be contingent upon the renouncement of idolatry and repentance for it

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r10.speaker: a third opinion
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r10.claim: A third view says the verse corrects Muslims who believed every major sinner belonged to the people of the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r10.anchor: According to a third opinion, this verse was revealed to correct a group of Muslims who held that anyone who committed a major sin

STUDYQURAN:39:53/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r11.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r11.claim: The Prophet says that if people did not sin and seek forgiveness, God would replace them with people who sin, seek forgiveness, and are forgiven.
STUDYQURAN:39:53/r11.anchor: the Prophet said, “If you did not sin [and seek forgiveness], God would remove you and come with a people who would sin

TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r1.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r1.claim: One reported view takes the address as people of idolatry who feared that past shirk, fornication, and murder would make faith useless and damn them.
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} [الزمر: 53]

TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Meccans wondered how they could migrate and become Muslim after worshipping idols and killing; the verse answered that they should not despair of God's mercy.
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} [الزمر: 53]

TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r3.claim: The command means not to despair: God forgives all sins, and the next verse urges people to return to their Lord and submit.
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r3.anchor: لا تيأسوا من رحمتي، إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا وقال: {وأنيبوا إلى ربكم وأسلموا له}

TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says believers are also admonished: if they sin, they must repent without delay, since obligations of lawful and unlawful conduct address the faithful.
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r4.anchor: وإنما الحلال والحرام لأهل الإيمان، فإياهم عاتب، وإياهم أمر إن أسرف أحدهم على نفسه

TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid explains the excess as killing a person in the pre-Islamic period.
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r5.anchor: مجاهد، في قول الله: {الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم} [الزمر: 53] قال: «قتل النفس في الجاهلية»

TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r6.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār that the three verses were revealed in Medina concerning Waḥshī and his companions.
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r6.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار، قال: " نزلت هذه الآيات الثلاث بالمدينة في وحشي وأصحابه

TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī links the believers' confession of sins and excess to this call to repentance, citing their prayer in Āl ʿImrān.
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r7.anchor: وقد ذكر الله في سورة آل عمران المؤمنين حين سألوا الله المغفرة، فقالوا:

TAB-FULL:v20p226/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r1.claim: Zayd b. Aslam says the address is specifically to polytheists.
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r1.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم، في قوله: {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} [الزمر: 53] قال: «إنما هي للمشركين»

TAB-FULL:v20p226/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r2.claim: Qatada reports that people with grave pre-Islamic sins feared Islam would bring them no repentance, so God addressed them with this verse.
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم} [الزمر: 53] حتى بلغ {الذنوب جميعا} [الزمر: 53]

TAB-FULL:v20p226/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Meccan polytheists asked how they could accept Islam after committing the very sins they were told would lead to ruin; the verse answered them.
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r3.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم} [الزمر: 53] قال: " هؤلاء المشركون من أهل مكة

TAB-FULL:v20p226/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says people condemned in pre-Islamic times considered following Muhammad but thought God and His Messenger would not accept them; the revelation continued through 39:58.
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} [الزمر: 53] الآية، قال: " كان قوم مسخوطين

TAB-FULL:v20p226/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r5.claim: Ibn Masud calls this the Qur'an's greatest verse of hope; Masruq reports that he affirmed Shutayr's statement.
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r5.anchor: سمعت ابن مسعود يقول: " إن أكبر آية فرجا في القرآن {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا}

TAB-FULL:v20p226/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r6.claim: Another group takes the verse to address Muslims and understands forgiveness of all sins as forgiveness for those God wills.
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عني بذلك أهل الإسلام، وقالوا: تأويل الكلام: إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء

TAB-FULL:v20p226/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r7.claim: This group says its qualification, “for whom He wills,” is also found in ʿAbd Allāh's codex.
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r7.anchor: قالوا: وهي كذلك في مصحف عبد الله

TAB-FULL:v20p226/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r8.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r8.claim: They say the verse was revealed about Muslims whom polytheists blocked from migrating and persecuted, leaving them afraid they had no repentance.
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r8.anchor: وقالوا: إنما نزلت هذه الآية في قوم صدهم المشركون عن الهجرة وفتنوهم، فأشفقوا أن لا يكون لهم توبة

TAB-FULL:v20p228/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r1.speaker: عمر
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r1.claim: Umar says persecuted converts thought apostasy under duress left no repentance; after the verse came, he wrote it to Hisham, who recognized its relevance and went to Medina.
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r1.anchor: قال يعني عمر: " كنا نقول: ما لمن افتتن من توبة؛ وكانوا يقولون: ما الله بقابل منا شيئا، تركنا الإسلام ببلاء أصابنا بعد معرفته

TAB-FULL:v20p228/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r2.claim: Ibn Umar says the verses concerned ʿAyyāsh, al-Walīd, and other Muslims tortured into apostasy; Umar sent them the revelation, and they returned to Islam and migrated.
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر، قال: " إنما أنزلت هذه الآيات في عياش بن أبي ربيعة، والوليد بن الوليد، ونفر من المسلمين

TAB-FULL:v20p228/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r3.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r3.claim: Ali calls 39:53 the Qur'an's broadest verse after others mention 4:110 and similar verses.
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r3.anchor: قال علي: " ما في القرآن آية أوسع من: {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم}

TAB-FULL:v20p228/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r4.claim: Ibn Masud rebukes a preacher who speaks only of Hell and shackles, asking whether he means to make people despair, and cites this verse.
TAB-FULL:v20p228/r4.anchor: فقال " ما يذكر أتقنط الناس؟ {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم}

TAB-FULL:v20p229/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r1.speaker: القرظي
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r1.claim: Al-Qurazi says the promise not to despair is for all people.
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r1.anchor: عن القرظي، أنه قال في هذه الآية: {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} [الزمر: 53] قال: «هي للناس أجمعين»

TAB-FULL:v20p229/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r2.claim: Thawban reports that the Prophet prized this verse above the world; when asked whether it included a polytheist, he affirmed it three times.
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r2.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " ما أحب أن لي الدنيا وما فيها بهذه الآية: {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله}

TAB-FULL:v20p229/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r3.claim: Another view says the verse addressed people who believed major sinners were Hell-bound, teaching that God forgives every sin for whomever He wills.
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: نزل ذلك في قوم كانوا يرون أهل الكبائر من أهل النار، فأعلمهم الله بذلك أنه يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء

TAB-FULL:v20p229/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r4.claim: Ibn Umar recounts that the Companions first feared major sins invalidated deeds (47:33), then after 4:48 they stopped declaring sinners doomed, fearing for sinners and hoping for others.
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر، قال: " كنا معشر أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نرى أو نقول: إنه ليس شيء من حسناتنا إلا وهي مقبولة

TAB-FULL:v20p229/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the address includes every transgressor, believer or polytheist, because its general wording does not single out one kind of sinner.
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r5.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: عنى تعالى ذكره بذلك جميع من أسرف على نفسه من أهل الإيمان والشرك، لأن الله عم بقوله

TAB-FULL:v20p229/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī recalls Ibn Masud's reading as qualifying forgiveness with “for whom He wills.”
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r6.anchor: كما قد ذكرنا قبل أن ابن مسعود كان يقرؤه

TAB-FULL:v20p229/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r7.claim: Shirk is forgiven when its perpetrator repents; unrepented shirk is excluded (4:48; 19:60), while other sins are subject to God's will, whether pardoned by grace or requited justly.
TAB-FULL:v20p229/r7.anchor: فأخبر أنه لا يغفر الشرك إلا بعد توبة بقوله: {إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا} [مريم: 60] فأما ما عداه فإن صاحبه في مشيئة ربه

TAB-FULL:v20p230/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p230/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p230/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “do not despair of God's mercy” as “do not lose hope in God's mercy.”
TAB-FULL:v20p230/r1.anchor: «لا تيأسوا من رحمة الله» كذلك: حدثني محمد بن سعد، قال: ثني أبي، قال: ثني عمي، قال: ثني أبي، عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس

SULAMI:v2p201#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r1.claim: God graciously gives servants until their last breath; even if they return to His door then, He will accept them.
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r1.anchor: قال سهل : امهل الله عباده تفضلا منه إلى آخر نفس فقال لهم : لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله

SULAMI:v2p201#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r2.claim: Junayd defines servanthood as turning away from whatever distracts one from worshipping one's Lord.
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد - رحمة الله عليه - : وقد سئل ما العبودية ؟ فقال : الإعراض عما يشغله من عبادة ربه .

SULAMI:v2p201#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r3.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r3.claim: Al-Jurayri says servants should neither rely on their worship and deeds nor despair over shortcomings, since divine care preceded worship.
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r3.anchor: قال الجريري : أمر الله عباده أن لا يعتمدوا العبادة والأعمال ولا يقنطوا من التقصير فيها

SULAMI:v2p201#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r4.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r4.claim: Yahya ibn Mu'adh calls this address one of the Qur'an's treasures that guarantees forgiveness for all believers.
SULAMI:v2p201#3/r4.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ : في كتاب الله كنوز موجبة للعفو عن جميع المؤمنين منها قوله : ﴿ يا عبادي

TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reports that after the verse urging sinners not to despair was revealed, a man asked the Prophet whether it included shirk; the Prophet disliked the question and cited this verse.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال لما نزلت { يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم } الآية فقام رجل

TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r3.speaker: أبو مجاز
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r3.claim: Abu Majaz says the Prophet was asked twice or thrice whether 39:53 covered shirk and stayed silent; then 4:48 descended, establishing one verse in each sura.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r3.anchor: عن أبي مجاز قال لما نزلت هذه الآية { يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا } الآية قام النبي صلى الله

TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r4.claim: The apparent context of 39:53 is forgiveness through repentance, which covers even shirk; 4:48 addresses a different case, so their meanings do not conflict and neither abrogates nor specifies the other.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r4.anchor: آية الزمر ظاهرة بحسب ما تتعقبه من الآيات في المغفرة بالتوبة ولا ريب أن التوبة يغفر معها كل ذنب حتى الشرك

TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r5.speaker: الكلبي
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verses were sent to Wahshi and companions after they regretted killing Hamza: they feared the repentance condition in 25:68–70, then feared God's will in 4:48, and entered Islam after 39:53 assured them.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#16/r5.anchor: عن الكلبي في الآية نزلت في المشركين وحشي وأصحابه وذلك أنه لما قتل حمزة

TABATABAI:4:44-58#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:44-58#17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:44-58#17/r1.claim: Al-Tabatabai judges the Wahshi account fabricated: its author lifts verses from separate contexts and rearranges them into an implausible extended exchange with the Prophet.
TABATABAI:4:44-58#17/r1.anchor: التأمل في موارد هذه الآيات التي تذكر الرواية أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يراجع بها وحشيا

TUSTARI:39:53/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:53/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:39:53/r1.claim: By grace God leaves room for repentance until the final breath and accepts those who return then; Sahl calls this the clearest verse of divine compassion, since God brings His servants into generosity through His prior remembrance of them.
TUSTARI:39:53/r1.anchor: أمهل الله تعالى عباده تفضلا منه إلى آخر نفس، فقال لهم

TUSTARI:39:53/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:53/r2.speaker: جبريل
TUSTARI:39:53/r2.claim: Gabriel tells Abraham that the generosity of God's pardon means He turns a forgiven sin into a good deed.
TUSTARI:39:53/r2.anchor: وقد حكي عن جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه سمع إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام يقول

TUSTARI:39:53/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:53/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:39:53/r3.claim: Sahl attests that his religion does not disavow sinful members of Muhammad's community, including killers, adulterers, and thieves, because God's special generosity toward this community cannot be fully measured.
TUSTARI:39:53/r3.anchor: اشهدوا علي أني من ديني أن لا أتبرأ من فساق أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وفجارهم وقاتلهم وزانيهم وسارقهم

TABATABAI:39:53/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.claim: The passage calls people to Islam and following revelation, warns of regret for excess and worldly arrogance, and contrasts the pious’ salvation with unbelievers’ loss; its tone conveys mercy.
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.anchor: أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يدعوهم إلى الإسلام واتباع ما أنزل الله ويحذرهم عما يستعقبه إسرافهم

TABATABAI:39:53/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53/r2.claim: Calling them His servants reminds them that God is their Lord and they owe Him obedience and worship, while the possessive address draws them toward His mercy and forgiveness.
TABATABAI:39:53/r2.anchor: ويناديهم بلفظة يا عبادي وفيه تذكير بحجة الله سبحانه على دعوتهم إلى عبادته

TABATABAI:39:53/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:39:53/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib defines isrāf as exceeding the limit in any human action, although the term is most commonly used for spending.
TABATABAI:39:53/r3.anchor: الإسراف - على ما ذكره الراغب - تجاوز الحد في كل فعل يفعله الإنسان وإن كان ذلك في الإنفاق أشهر

TABATABAI:39:53/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53/r4.claim: The construction implies wrongdoing against oneself; in context, excess means sinning, whether through shirk or other major or minor sins.
TABATABAI:39:53/r4.anchor: والإسراف على النفس هو التعدي عليها باقتراف الذنب أعم من الشرك وسائر الذنوب الكبيرة والصغيرة

TABATABAI:39:53/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r5.speaker: جمع
TABATABAI:39:53/r5.claim: A group takes My servants to mean sinful believers, since the Qur’an often uses the divine possessive address for believers.
TABATABAI:39:53/r5.anchor: وقال جمع إن المراد بالعباد المؤمنون وقد غلب استعماله فيهم مضافا إليه تعالى في القرآن

TABATABAI:39:53/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53/r6.claim: The continuous seven-verse context, ending with explicit denial and arrogance, includes polytheists; Qur’anic uses of My servants for believers are contextually marked rather than the default meaning.
TABATABAI:39:53/r6.anchor: إلى تمام سبع آيات ذو سياق واحد متصل يفصح عن دعوتهم

TABATABAI:39:53/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:39:53/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī affirms that the address includes polytheists, while finding Ibn ʿAbbās’s polytheists-only reading more plausible than restricting it to believers.
TABATABAI:39:53/r7.anchor: والقول بأن المراد به المشركون خاصة نظرا إلى سياق الآيات كما نقل عن ابن عباس أقرب إلى القبول

TABATABAI:39:53/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53/r8.anchor: القنوط اليأس، والمراد بالرحمة بقرينة خطاب المذنبين

TABATABAI:39:53/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53/r9.claim: Here mercy means the mercy of the afterlife; for sinners being called to repent, its immediate relevant aspect is forgiveness.
TABATABAI:39:53/r9.anchor: والمراد بالرحمة بقرينة خطاب المذنبين ودعوتهم هو الرحمة المتعلقة بالآخرة دون ما هي أعم

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r1.claim: The shift from first-person speech to saying God forgives points to God’s beautiful names, especially the Forgiving and Merciful: He forgives because He is God.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r1.anchor: وفي الآية التفات من التكلم إلى الغيبة حيث قيل

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r2.claim: All sins are eligible for forgiveness, but forgiveness requires a specific cause and is not arbitrary; the Qur’an recognizes intercession and repentance as causes.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r2.anchor: إعلام بأن جميع الذنوب قابلة للمغفرة فالمغفرة عامة لكنها تحتاج إلى سبب مخصص ولا تكون جزافا

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r3.claim: He rejects intercession as the forgiveness meant here because Qur’anic passages exclude shirk from intercession, whereas this verse addresses shirk as well as other sins.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r3.anchor: المغفرة الحاصلة بالشفاعة لأن الشفاعة لا تنال الشرك بنص القرآن في آيات كثيرة

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.claim: These seven verses form one connected discourse: the ban on despair prepares for the following calls to repentance, submission, and righteous action, so the first verse is not an isolated promise.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.anchor: كلام واحد ذو سياق واحد متصل ينهى عن القنوط

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r5.speaker: قوم
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r5.claim: One group restricts the general forgiveness to shirk and major sins threatened with punishment, without requiring repentance, and concludes that only minor sins are forgiven.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r5.anchor: فقد ذهب قوم إلى تقييد عموم المغفرة فيها بالشرك وسائر الكبائر التي وعد الله عليها النار مع عدم تقييد العموم بالتوبة

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r6.speaker: آخرون
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r6.claim: Another group leaves forgiveness unrestricted and without a cause, except for shirk, using 4:116 to infer arbitrary forgiveness for other sins.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r6.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى إطلاق المغفرة وعدم تقيدها بالتوبة ولا بسبب آخر من أسباب المغفرة غير أنهم قيدوها بالشرك

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r7.claim: Since God’s statement in 4:116 concerns shirk and other sins and states shirk is not forgiven except through repentance, the unrestricted reading must be qualified by repentance.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r7.anchor: ومن المعلوم من كلامه تعالى أن الشرك لا يغفر إلا بالتوبة فتقيد إطلاق المغفرة في الآية بالتوبة مما لا مفر منه

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r8.claim: God’s speech explicitly allows repentance to bring forgiveness for every sin, including shirk.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r8.anchor: وكلامه تعالى صريح في مغفرة الذنوب جميعا حتى الشرك بالتوبة

TABATABAI:39:57-61/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r10.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r10.claim: A report from ʿAlī says no Qur’anic verse is broader than the call My servants who have transgressed against themselves; another report from him calls 93:5 more hope-giving.
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r10.anchor: عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أنه قال ما في القرآن آية أوسع من

TABATABAI:39:53-61/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r1.claim: In Thawban’s report, the Prophet said he would not trade the world for this verse; when asked about one who associates partners, he paused and said except one who associates.
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r1.anchor: فسكت النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ثم قال إلا من أشرك

TABATABAI:39:53-61/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r2.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r2.claim: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī reports the Prophet saying that if people did not sin, God would create a people who sinned and were forgiven.
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r2.anchor: عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول

TABATABAI:39:53-61/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the forgiveness in the report about sinners does not rule out its being conditioned on causes such as repentance or intercession.
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r3.anchor: أقول ما في الحديث من المغفرة لا يأبى التقيد بأسباب المغفرة كالتوبة والشفاعة

TABATABAI:39:53-61/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r4.claim: A report in al-Majmaʿ says the verse came when Waḥshī, Ḥamza’s killer, feared his conversion would not be accepted; he converted, and the Prophet said the verse was for all Muslims.
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r4.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:39:53-61/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r5.speaker: تفسير الكلبي
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r5.claim: In al-Kalbī’s account, Waḥshī and companions fear that prior shirk, murder, and adultery bar conversion; after successive Qur’anic assurances and their conversion, the Prophet tells Waḥshī to stay away, and he later dies after long-term drinking.
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r5.anchor: وعن كتاب سعد السعود لابن طاوس نقلا عن تفسير الكلبي

TABATABAI:39:53-61/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r6.claim: He weakens the Wahshī occasion report because the sūra is Meccan whereas Wahshī converted after the Hijra; the report also implies unconditioned forgiveness, which the context excludes.
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r6.anchor: ويضعفه أن السورة مكية وقد أسلم وحشي بعد الهجرة

TABATABAI:39:53-61/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r7.claim: He notes that al-khamr might be a place-name near Medina, perhaps a copyist’s error for al-Ḥimṣ, or a reference to Waḥshī dying from drinking; he says Waḥshī was a habitual drinker who later quit.
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r7.anchor: لعله بفتح الخاء وتشديد الميم موضع من أعراض المدينة ولعله من غلط الناسخ

TABATABAI:39:53-61/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r8.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r8.claim: Many reports from the Imams apply these verses to their Shiʿa and identify the side of God with them; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī classifies these as instances of application, not exegesis.
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r8.anchor: هناك روايات كثيرة عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام في تطبيق هذه الآيات على شيعتهم وتطبيق جنب الله عليهم وهي جميعا من الجري دون التفسير

TABRISI:39:51-55/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:51-55/r8.claim: Those who went to excess against themselves committed sins; they must not despair of forgiveness.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r8.anchor: بارتكاب الذنوب { لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله } أي لا تيأسوا من مغفرة الله

TABRISI:39:51-55/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:51-55/r9.claim: God certainly forgives all sins for the repentant; an unrepentant monotheist remains under God’s will, who may punish or forgive.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r9.anchor: فالله سبحانه يغفر جميع الذنوب للتائب لا محالة فإن مات الموحد من غير توبة فهو في مشيئة الله

TABRISI:39:51-55/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r10.speaker: ثوبان مولى رسول الله
TABRISI:39:51-55/r10.claim: Thawbān, the Messenger’s client, said he would not trade the whole world for this verse.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r10.anchor: وعن ثوبان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:39:51-55/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r11.speaker: علي
TABRISI:39:51-55/r11.claim: ʿAlī said no Qurʾānic verse is broader than this verse.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r11.anchor: وعن أمير المؤمنين علي ع أنه قال: ما في القرآن آية أوسع من

TABRISI:39:51-55/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r12.speaker: عبد الله
TABRISI:39:51-55/r12.claim: ʿAbd Allāh’s codex adds ‘for whomever He wills.’
TABRISI:39:51-55/r12.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله أن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء

TABRISI:39:51-55/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:51-55/r13.claim: A reported occasion says the verse was revealed about Waḥshī, who feared his repentance would be rejected; the Prophet said it applies to all Muslims.
