The author rejects the chronology because the verse is Meccan and Waḥshī converted later, though it may have been recited to him and prompted his Islam.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r13.anchor: نزلت في وحشي قاتل حمزة حين أراد أن يسلم وخاف أن لا تقبل توبته

TABRISI:39:51-55/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:51-55/r14.claim: The unrepentant monotheist’s case is linked to 4:48, God forgives lesser sins for whom He wills.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r14.anchor: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء

FARRA:v2p421/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p421/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v2p421/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas read the phrase as in Abdullah’s codex, adding لمن يشاء.
FARRA:v2p421/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: وحدثني أبو إسحاق التيمي عن أبي روق عن إبراهيم التيمي عن ابن عباس أنه قرأها كما هي في مصحف عبد الله (يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء)

FARRA:v2p421/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p421/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p421/r2.claim: Farra says the passage was revealed concerning Wahshi, Hamza’s killer, and his associates.
FARRA:v2p421/r2.anchor: وإنما نزلت في وحشي قاتل حمزة وذويه.

THALABI:v8p240#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p240#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p240#2/r1.claim: Interpreters differ about whom the address to those who have sinned greatly concerns.
THALABI:v8p240#2/r1.anchor: اختلف المفسرون في المعنيين بهذه الآية. فقال بعضهم: عنى بها قوما من المشركين.

THALABI:v8p240#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p240#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p240#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Meccans who feared they could not migrate and submit after idolatry and unlawful killing, since they thought Muhammad said such sins would never be forgiven.
THALABI:v8p240#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في أهل مكة قالوا يزعم محمد انه من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس التي حرم الله لم يغفر له،

THALABI:v8p240#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p240#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p240#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet invited Wahshi to Islam; Wahshi asked whether there was a dispensation for his murder, associationism, and fornication, and the verse promising forgiveness to repentant believers was revealed.
THALABI:v8p240#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى وحشي يدعوه إلى الإسلام، فأرسل إليه: يا محمد كيف تدعوني إلى دينك

THALABI:v8p241/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p241/r1.speaker: وحشي
THALABI:v8p241/r1.claim: Wahshi says the conditions of repentance and then the warning about unpardoned association were too hard; after this verse was revealed he accepted Islam, and the Prophet said its promise applies to Muslims generally.
THALABI:v8p241/r1.anchor: قال وحشي: هذا شرط شديد فلعلي لا أقدر على هذا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء.

THALABI:v8p241/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p241/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p241/r2.claim: Qatada reports that people with grave pre-Islamic sins feared they would not be accepted as converts, so God called them with this verse.
THALABI:v8p241/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة ذكر لنا أن ناسا أصابوا ذنوبا عظاما في الجاهلية، فلما جاء الإسلام أشفقوا أن لن يتاب عليهم، فدعاهم الله بهذه الآية.

THALABI:v8p241/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p241/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v8p241/r3.claim: Ibn Umar says the verses concerned Ayyash ibn Abi Rabiʿa, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and other Muslims who reverted under torture; Umar wrote them the verses, after which they returned to Islam and migrated.
THALABI:v8p241/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: نزلت هذه الآيات في عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر من المسلمين، كانوا أسلموا ثم فتنوا وعذبوا فافتتنوا

THALABI:v8p241/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p241/r4.speaker: عمر عن ابن عمر
THALABI:v8p241/r4.claim: Umar recounts that he, Ayyash, and Hisham set out to migrate together; Hisham was detained and apostatized under pressure, and the Muslims then feared that people who reverted under worldly coercion could not repent.
THALABI:v8p241/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قال: لما اجتمعنا إلى الهجرة أبعدت أنا وعياش بن أبي ربيعة وهشام بن العاص بن وائل وقلنا: الميعاد بيننا

THALABI:v8p242/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p242/r1.speaker: عمر
THALABI:v8p242/r1.claim: Umar wrote the verse to Hisham; Hisham understood it as revealed about their situation, rejoined the Prophet, and later died at Ajnadayn during Abu Bakr's rule.
THALABI:v8p242/r1.anchor: قال عمر: فكتبتها بيدي كتابا ثم بعثت بها إلى هشام. قال هشام: فلما قدمت علي خرجت بها إلى ذي طوى فقلت اللهم فهمنيها، فعرفت أنها أنزلت فينا،

THALABI:v8p242/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p242/r2.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v8p242/r2.claim: Some say the verse addressed those who regarded people guilty of major sins as destined for Hell; God taught that He may forgive every sin for whom He wills.
THALABI:v8p242/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: نزلت في قوم كانوا يرون أهل الكبائر من أهل النار، فأعلمهم الله تعالى أنه يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء.

THALABI:v8p242/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p242/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان عن نافع عن ابن عمر
THALABI:v8p242/r3.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Companions once feared major sins and indecencies invalidated good deeds, then this verse stopped them from declaring sinners doomed; they thereafter feared for sinners and hoped for others.
THALABI:v8p242/r3.anchor: وروى مقاتل بن حيان عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: كنا معشر أصحاب رسول الله نرى أو نقول: أنه ليس شيء من حسناتنا إلا وهي مقبولة حتى نزلت هذه الآية أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول ولا تبطلوا أعمالكم

THALABI:v8p242/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p242/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p242/r4.claim: Here extravagance means committing major sins, and the address not to despair applies generally to all people.
THALABI:v8p242/r4.anchor: وأراد بالإسراف ارتكاب الكبائر، والآية عامة للناس أجمعين لا تقنطوا.

THALABI:v8p242/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p242/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وعيسى والكسائي ويعقوب
THALABI:v8p242/r5.claim: Abu Amr, al-Aʿmash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Isa, al-Kisaʾi, and Yaqub read the nūn of taqnaṭū with kasra.
THALABI:v8p242/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وعيسى والكسائي ويعقوب (لا تقنطوا) بكسر النون.

THALABI:v8p242/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p242/r6.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
THALABI:v8p242/r6.claim: Ashhab al-Uqayli reads the nūn with ḍamma.

THALABI:v8p242/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p242/r7.speaker: الآخرون
THALABI:v8p242/r7.claim: The other readers use fatḥ on the nūn.

THALABI:v8p242/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p242/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v8p242/r8.claim: Ibn Masud rebuked a preacher dwelling on Hell and shackles for making people despair, then recited the promise not to despair of God's mercy.
THALABI:v8p242/r8.anchor: عن أبي الكنود قال: دخل عبد الله بن مسعود المسجد فإذا قاص يقص وهو يذكر النار والأغلال، فجاء حتى قام على رأسه وقال: يا مذكر لم تقنط الناس

THALABI:v8p242/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p242/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v8p242/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam tells of an earlier worshipper who imposed hardship on himself and made others despair of mercy; when he died, God told him his destination was the Fire, prompting him to ask about his devotion.
THALABI:v8p242/r9.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم: أن رجلا كان في الأمم الماضية يجتهد في العبادة فيشدد على نفسه ويقنط الناس من رحمة الله ثم مات فقال: أي رب ما لي عندك؟ قال: النار.

THALABI:v8p243/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p243/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p243/r1.claim: God tells the person who made others despair of His mercy in worldly life that He will make him despair of His mercy today.
THALABI:v8p243/r1.anchor: إنك كنت تقنط الناس من رحمتي في الدنيا، فأنا اليوم أقنطك من رحمتي.

THALABI:v8p243/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p243/r2.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد
THALABI:v8p243/r2.claim: Asma bint Yazid reports that the Prophet recited the verse and added that God forgives all sins without concern; no grading is given.
THALABI:v8p243/r2.anchor: عن أسماء بنت يزيد قالت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v8p243/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p243/r3.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v8p243/r3.claim: A reading in the codex of Abdullah adds that God forgives all sins for whomever He wills.
THALABI:v8p243/r3.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله: (إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء)

THALABI:v8p243/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p243/r4.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
THALABI:v8p243/r4.claim: Abu al-Jawza says he knew no scholar or Companion of Muhammad who declared that God would not forgive a particular sin; no grading is given.
THALABI:v8p243/r4.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء قال: ما علمت أحدا من أهل العلم

THALABI:v8p243/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p243/r5.speaker: ثوبان
THALABI:v8p243/r5.claim: Thawban reports that the Prophet prized this verse above the world; when asked whether it included one who associated partners, he answered yes three times.
THALABI:v8p243/r5.anchor: أنه سمع ثوبان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: سمعت رسول الله

THALABI:v8p243/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p243/r6.speaker: علي
THALABI:v8p243/r6.claim: Ibn Sirin reports Ali's judgment that no Qur'anic verse is more expansive in hope than this verse.
THALABI:v8p243/r6.anchor: عن ابن سيرين قال: قال علي رضي الله عنه: ما في القرآن آية أوسع

THALABI:v8p243/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p243/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v8p243/r7.claim: Sha'tir ibn Shakl reports Ibn Masud calling this the Qur'an's most hope-giving verse.
THALABI:v8p243/r7.anchor: عن شتير بن شكل قال: سمعت ابن مسعود يقول: إن أكثر آية فرجا

THALABI:v8p244/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p244/r1.speaker: الزهري
THALABI:v8p244/r1.claim: Al-Zuhri tells how Umar brought a weeping youth to the Prophet; the youth confessed grave robbery and intercourse with a corpse, and the Prophet taught that God forgives immense sins absent shirk or murder. No grading is stated.
THALABI:v8p244/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن الزهري قال: دخل عمر بن الخطاب على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v8p245/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p245/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p245/r1.claim: The continuation says Gabriel relayed God's questions about who created, provides for, and accepts repentance from creatures; God ordered the youth forgiven, and the Prophet accepted his repentance.
THALABI:v8p245/r1.anchor: فدعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الشاب فتاب عليه وقال:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r1.claim: Those who went to excess against themselves committed major sins and shameful acts.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r2.claim: Some Meccans intended to embrace Islam but feared their past idolatry, associating partners, and killing could not be forgiven; God revealed that whoever repents and believes can be forgiven every sin.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r2.anchor: نزلت في قوم من أهل مكة هموا بالإسلام، ثم قالوا:

ELMALILI:39:53-55/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r1.claim: Israf usually means spending money excessively, but more broadly it is exceeding bounds in any act; here it includes wronging one's own soul through excessive sin.
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r1.anchor: “İsrâf” mal sarfında meşhur ise de insanın yaptığı herhangi bir fiilde haddini aşmaktır.

ELMALILI:39:53-55/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r2.claim: The preposition ʿalā incorporates the sense of committing a crime against oneself into the phrase.
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r2.anchor: Burada cinayet mânası da tazmin olunarak عَلَىٰٓ ile sılalanmıştır.

ELMALILI:39:53-55/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r3.claim: Though called the Qur'an's most hopeful verse, its hope is meant to urge even the greatest sinners to repent immediately, not to encourage sin.
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r3.anchor: Bu âyetin Kur’an’da en ümidli âyet olduğu söylenir. Bununla beraber dikkat edilmek lâzım gelir ki bu ümid, günaha teşvik için değil

ELMALILI:39:53-55/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r4.speaker: Atâ b. Yesâr
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r4.claim: Atā ibn Yasār reports that the verse was revealed in Medina concerning Wahshi, the killer of Hamza.
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r4.anchor: Atâ b. Yesâr’dan[^1] olan rivayete göre

ELMALILI:39:53-55/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r5.speaker: İbn Ömer
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r5.claim: Ibn Umar reports that tortured converts Ayyaash, Walid ibn Walid and others who had renounced Islam received the verse through Umar's handwritten letter and then returned to Islam and emigrated.
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r5.anchor: İbn Ömer’den rivayet olunduğuna göre de demiştir ki: “Ayyaş b. Ebî Rebî‘a ve Velîd b. Velîd ve daha birkaç nefer Müslüman olmuşlardı.

ELMALILI:39:53-55/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r6.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Meccans asked how they could convert after idolatry and murder if Muhammad claimed such sins were unforgiven; God then revealed this verse.
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r6.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayet olunduğuna göre de Mekkeliler şöyle demişler: “Muhammed zu‘mediyor ki putlara tapan

ELMALILI:39:53-55/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r7.claim: Although the reported occasion concerns unbelievers entering Islam, the verse also includes sinful believers' repentance, all the more so.
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r7.anchor: sebeb-i nüzul kâfirlerin islâmı meselesi ise de mefhum âsîlerin tevbesine de şâmil olduğunda şüphe yoktur

ELMALILI:39:53-55/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r8.claim: The statement that God does not forgive associating partners with Him means unrepented shirk; repentance makes forgiveness possible.
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r8.anchor: âyeti mûcebince şirkin mağfiret olunmaması tevbe edilmediği takdirdedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r1.claim: “Transgressing” means plunging into sins and violating God’s commands.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r1.anchor: “Haddi aşmak”tan maksat, günahlara dalarak Allah’ın hükümlerini çiğnemektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r2.claim: The phrase “against themselves” highlights that sinners first soil their own souls and lives and thereby harm themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r2.anchor: “Kendi aleyhlerine olarak” diye çevirdiğimiz alâ enfüsihim deyimiyle, günah işleyen kişinin, her şeyden önce kendi ruhunu ve hayatını kirletmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r3.claim: The verse is an unmistakable divine promise that God’s mercy and forgiveness are so vast that despair is never warranted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r3.anchor: Bu âyet, Allah’ın rahmet ve affının asla ümitsizliğe izin vermeyecek derecede geniş olduğunu en açık bir şekilde ortaya koyan ilâhî müjde olarak değerlendirilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r4.claim: No power can constrain God’s will, so his capacity to forgive cannot be limited by fixed conditions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r4.anchor: Allah’ın iradesini sınırlayacak hiçbir güç bulunmadığı için O’nun bağışlama yetkisine belli şartlarla sahip olduğu gibi bir görüş de ileri sürülemez.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r5.claim: Reading “God forgives all sins” as a promise to forgive everyone regardless of faith, repentance, or turning to God would invite religious and moral laxity, even anarchy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r5.anchor: inanan inanmayan, tövbe eden etmeyen, kendisine yönelen yönelmeyen herkesi bağışlayacağını düşünmek, kaçınılmaz olarak dinî ve ahlâkî gevşekliğe hatta anarşiye yol açar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r6.claim: A Qur’anic verse should not be read in isolation from the whole, since doing so can cause serious errors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r6.anchor: kural olarak Kur’an’ın bir âyetini bütününden kopararak tek başına değerlendirmek ciddi yanlışlar doğurabilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r7.claim: Nisa 4:48 and 4:116 say God never forgives associating partners with him, while other sins are forgiven for whomever he wills; thus forgiveness is not unconditional.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r7.anchor: Nisâ sûresinin 48 ve 116. âyetlerinde aynı ifadelerle, “Allah kendisine ortak koşulmasını asla bağışlamaz; bundan başkasını dilediği kimse hakkında bağışlar” buyurulmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r8.claim: To prevent misunderstanding, the authors chose to make the implied condition “if He wills” explicit in their translation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r8.anchor: Yanlış anlama ihtimalini önlemek düşüncesiyle konumuz olan âyetin meâlinde bu şartı (dilerse) şeklinde göstermeyi yararlı gördük.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r9.claim: The next verse indicates that deserving God’s forgiveness first requires turning to him and submitting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r9.anchor: Esasen bir sonraki âyet de Allah’ın affına lâyık olabilmek için her şeyden önce O’na yönelip teslim olmak gerektiğine işaret etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r10.speaker: Ehl-i sünnet âlimleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r10.claim: Sunni scholars hold that forgiveness is not conditional on repentance and argue that imposing this condition arbitrarily narrows the verse’s scope.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:53/r10.anchor: Ehl-i sünnet âlimleri, affın tövbe şartına bağlı olmadığını belirtmişler; bu şartı ileri sürenlerin keyfî olarak âyetin kapsamını daralttıklarını savunmuşlardır

BURHAN:v1p404/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p404/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p404/r5.claim: The preserved yāʾ and vocative in the call to servants who exceeded the bounds summon them from Islam and obedience toward the station of spiritual excellence; the author gives a similar reading for believers in al-ʿAnkabūt.
BURHAN:v1p404/r5.anchor: وكذلك ﴿ يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على ﴾ ثبت الضمير وحرف النداء فى الخط فإنه دعاهم

BURHAN:v1p202/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p202/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p202/r1.claim: Zarkashi classifies Surat al-Zumar as Meccan except the verse calling the servants who have sinned not to despair of God’s mercy.
BURHAN:v1p202/r1.anchor: سورة الزمر مكية غير قوله ﴿ قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم ﴾ الآية

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r1.speaker: author
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r1.claim: Al-Suyūṭī refers to the report from the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections already cited in his discussion of Surat al-Furqān.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا ﴾ الآية تقدم حديث الشيخين في سورة الفرقان

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports with an explicitly sound chain that this verse was revealed concerning the polytheists of Mecca.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r2.anchor: وأخرج بن أبي حاتم بسند صحيح عن ابن عباس قال أنزلت هذه الآية في مشركي أهل مكة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says they had thought there was no repentance for one who apostatized after knowing Islam; when the Prophet arrived in Medina, this verse was revealed about them.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r3.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم والطبراني عن ابن عمر قال كنا نقول ما لمفتتن توبة إذا ترك دينه بعد إسلامه ومعرفته

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r4.speaker: وحشي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r4.claim: When invited to Islam, Wahshī objected that he had killed, committed adultery, and associated partners; after earlier verses and the discretionary forgiveness verse seemed conditional, this universal call reassured him and he converted.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p185/r4.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني بسند فيه ضعف عن ابن عباس قال بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى وحشي قاتل حمزة يدعوه إلى الإسلام

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Meccans who feared that idol worship and killing a protected person would remain unforgiven, and asked why they should migrate and become Muslims.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في أهل مكة قالوا: يزعم محمد أن من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس التي حرم الله لم يغفر له

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r2.claim: Ibn Umar says it concerned Ayyash ibn Abi Rabiah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and Muslims tortured into apostasy; Umar wrote to them with the verses, and they returned to Islam and migrated.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: نزلت هذه الآية في عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر من المسلمين كانوا أسلموا ثم فتنوا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Sa'id ibn Jubayr, reports that polytheists who had committed many murders and acts of fornication asked the Prophet whether their past deeds could be expiated; al-Bukhari transmits this report.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن ناسا من أهل الشرك كانوا قد قتلوا فأكثروا، وزنوا فأكثروا، ثم أتوا محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r4.speaker: عمر
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r4.claim: Umar recounts that he, Ayyash, and Hisham planned to migrate together; Hisham was detained and tortured into apostasy, so Umar sent him the revealed verses, which led Hisham to return to the Prophet.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن عمر أنه قال: لما اجتمعنا إلى الهجرة اتعدت أنا وعياش بن أبي ربيعة

BURHAN:v3p180/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p180/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p180/r1.claim: The vocative often drops the yāʾ attached to the first-person pronoun because calling favors omission; Qur'anic forms also retain it with sukūn or fatḥa, or replace it with alif.
BURHAN:v3p180/r1.anchor: باب حذف ألا ترى أنه يحذف منه التنوين وبعض الاسم

BURHAN:v2p118/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p118/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p118/r5.claim: The tender address in 39:53 is designed to win hearts and encourage people to embrace Islam.
BURHAN:v2p118/r5.anchor: وأما بالنسبة إلى المقامات فانظر إلى مقام الترغيب وإلى مقام الترهيب

BURHAN:v2p118/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p118/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p118/r6.claim: An unnamed report says Ayyash, al-Walid b. al-Walid, and others reverted under torture; ʿUmar sent them the verse, and they returned to Islam and emigrated.
BURHAN:v2p118/r6.anchor: قيل وكان سبب نزولها أنه أسلم عياش بن أبى ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر معهما ثم فتنوا وعذبوا فافتتنوا

BURHAN:v2p118/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p118/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p118/r7.claim: The general promise of forgiveness is qualified by 4:48, so it cannot imply forgiveness of shirk; the promise applies to other sins.

BURHAN:v2p118/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p118/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p118/r8.claim: The Qur'an uses عباد when annexed to God for believers, as in 76:6; the author asks how those being urged were not believers.
BURHAN:v2p118/r8.anchor: ومنها أن لفظ العباد مضافا إليه فى القرآن مخصوص بالمؤمنين قال تعالى ﴿ عينا يشرب بها عباد الله ﴾

BURHAN:v1p446/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p446/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
BURHAN:v1p446/r11.claim: In al-Hakim’s report from Ibn al-Munkadir, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr names God’s call to those who have transgressed as the most hopeful verse.
BURHAN:v1p446/r11.anchor: التقى ابن عباس وعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص فقال ابن عباس

BURHAN:v4p421/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p421/r5.speaker: الأخفش
BURHAN:v4p421/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash allows زائد من in affirmative wording; here it means all sins, as confirmed by إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا, so the first verse is read with زائد من to avoid contradiction.

ITQAN:v3p92/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p92/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p92/r1.claim: The Qur'an uses a tender, solicitous address, exemplified by “My servants who have transgressed against themselves.”
ITQAN:v3p92/r1.anchor: الثلاثون خطاب التحنن والإستعطاف نحو ﴿ يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا ﴾

ITQAN:v1p52/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p52/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p52/r3.claim: The three “Say, My servants” verses are listed as Medinan exceptions in al-Zumar, following the earlier report from Ibn Abbas.
ITQAN:v1p52/r3.anchor: الآيات الثلاث كما تقدم عن ابن عباس

ITQAN:v1p52/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p52/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p52/r4.claim: Another route from Ibn Abbas says the “Say, My servants” passage was revealed about Wahshi, Hamza’s killer.
ITQAN:v1p52/r4.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني من وجه آخر عنه أنها نزلت في وحشي قاتل حمزة

ITQAN:v4p426/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p426/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p426/r9.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits Ibn Masʿud calling 39:53 the verse that gives the greatest hope.
ITQAN:v4p426/r9.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني عنه قال ما في القرآن آية أعظم فرجا من آية في سورة الغرف

ITQAN:v4p426/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p426/r14.speaker: رسول الله ﷺ
ITQAN:v4p426/r14.claim: The same Prophetic report calls 39:53 the most hopeful verse.
ITQAN:v4p426/r14.anchor: وأرجى آية في القرآن ﴿ قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم

DAMGHANI:v1p235/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p235/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p235/r10.claim: Asrafū can mean going to excess and committing many sins.
DAMGHANI:v1p235/r10.anchor: الإسراف الإفراط في المعاصي والإكثار منها قوله تعالى في سورة الزمر

DAMGHANI:v1p314/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p314/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p314/r5.claim: ʿIbād can mean slaves or servants, as in God's servants, the servants attributed to God, and household slaves.
DAMGHANI:v1p314/r5.anchor: العباد المماليك قوله تعالى في سورة الزمر

NAHHAS:v4p15/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p15/r7.claim: The yāʾ may be omitted because vocatives permit deletion.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r7.anchor: وإن شئت حذفت الياء لأن النداء موضع حذف

NAHHAS:v4p15/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
NAHHAS:v4p15/r8.claim: Ibn Umar recounts the Hijra rendezvous, Hisham's detention and apostasy, and believers' fear those tested had no repentance; then the verse was revealed.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r8.anchor: ما رواه محمد بن إسحاق عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال لما اجتمعنا على الهجرة

NAHHAS:v4p15/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p15/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says idolaters who killed and committed adultery in excess asked whether they could repent, and this passage was revealed.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r9.anchor: وروى عبد الأعلى عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال كان قوم من المشركين

NAHHAS:v4p15/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر وابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p15/r10.claim: Ibn Umar calls this the most hopeful verse; Ibn Abbas counters with 11:114.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r10.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر هذه أرجى آية في القرآن فرد عليه ابن عباس

NAHHAS:v4p15/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r11.speaker: أسماء
NAHHAS:v4p15/r11.claim: Asma says she heard the Prophet recite an added ولا يبالي in the verse's ending.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r11.anchor: عن أسماء أنها سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ

NAHHAS:v4p15/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
NAHHAS:v4p15/r12.claim: Ibn Masud's codex reads إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء; al-Nahhas treats both forms as explanatory glosses.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r12.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود ( إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء ) وهاتان القراءتان على التفسير

NAHHAS:v4p15/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p15/r13.claim: The intended recipients are penitents or people with minor but no major sins; the next verse points to penitence.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r13.anchor: وقد عرف الله جل وعز من يشاء أن يغفر له وهو التائب أو من عمل صغيرة ولم يكن له كبيرة

ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r6.claim: Qanata means to despair; the command not to despair means not to lose hope.

ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r7.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r7.claim: Tafsir reports that people in Mecca thought idolatry, associating partners with God, and murder were unforgivable; God declares that anyone who repents and believes can be forgiven all sins.
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r7.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن قوما من أهل مكة قالوا إن محمدا يقول: إن من عبد الأوثان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r2.claim: The sinners addressed in قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا are numerous, which fits the full form with the explicit yā.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r2.anchor: بذكر الياء لأن المسرفون هم كثر لذا جاءت عبادي بياء المتكلم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.claim: The next section warns that polytheism and intercession will not save the idolaters but hasten ruin; success requires sincere turning to God and following His revealed Book, or their later regret will be useless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.anchor: The path to success hinges on focussing attention towards God with sincerity of heart and on following this best of Books

NASHR:v2p170/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p170/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p170/r1.claim: Across fourteen disputed yāʾs before hamzat waṣl plus the definite article, Ḥamza alone sukunizes every yāʾ.
NASHR:v2p170/r1.anchor: والمختلف فيه من ذلك أربع عشرة ياء: في البقرة ثنتان لا ينال عهدي الظالمين،

NASHR:v2p170/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p170/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p170/r2.claim: Additional sukun readings are reported for Ḥafṣ at عهدي الظالمين, Ibn ʿĀmir at آياتي الذين, and Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Kisāʾī, and Rawḥ at قل لعبادي الذين.
NASHR:v2p170/r2.anchor: ووافقه حفص في عهدي الظالمين، وابن عامر في آياتي الذين في الأعراف، وابن عامر والكسائي

NASHR:v2p170/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p170/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p170/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, Yaʿqūb, and Khalaf also sukunize the yāʾ in يا عبادي الذين آمنوا in al-ʿAnkabūt and al-Zumar.
NASHR:v2p170/r3.anchor: وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب وخلف في ياعبادي الذين آمنوا في العنكبوت والزمر

NASHR:v2p170/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p170/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p170/r5.claim: The readers agree to fatḥa on the remaining eighteen yāʾs in this section.
NASHR:v2p170/r5.anchor: على فتح ما بقي من هذا الفصل، وهو ثماني عشرة ياء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1059/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1059/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1059/r2.claim: Those who sin are numerous, as other verses say most people do not believe or follow guidance, which suits the expanded form عبادي.
